reviews.author: ethan ghymn
reviews.text:
I think I saw this store on Instagram, but when I looked at Manple, I saw that it was a new store and it wasn't registered, so I registered it and saved it in I want to go.

I wanted to eat Korean food today, but this place reminded me of Hwangtaeil-ro, so I decided to stop by.

Now, I eat meat soup to some extent, but only when I am confident about the quality of the meat. When I was young, I was particularly sensitive to meat. It was nice to be able to eat soup with non-meat ingredients, such as pollack soup, and I still like it. I stopped by Mugyo Dongbuk Fish Guk House and Seonyudo Station Original Pollack Soup, but it was a shame that it didn't meet my expectations, but the prices here are relatively high, so I headed to the store, wondering if it would live up to my expectations.

Looking at the reviews here and there, the store felt like a more upscale version of the old Mangwon-dong Aban, but when I stood in front of the store, it was relatively empty since it was about 1 o'clock after the peak lunch hour. As soon as I entered the store, I ordered at the kiosk on the left, and it was different from the regular Hwanggomtang. When I inquired about the difference, I was told that it had more broth and more dried pollack, so I ordered the regular Hwanggomtang and the Hwangtae Rolled Dumpling, which were said to be good in reviews. I sat in the counter seats only.

On the counter, there is a pitcher of barley tea and Cheongyang peppers, salted shrimp, and pepper ready to be added to the yellow gomtang according to your taste.

First, the dried pollack soup was prepared, and soon after, the dried dried pollack dumplings were served with homemade sauce. To taste the dried pollack dumplings, I picked one up and dipped it in the sauce. There was quite a lot of sauce, so I felt like I was dipping it in. When I dipped it in and tasted it, it was a savory peanut sauce or horseradish sauce base that is commonly used when eating Chinese cold noodles, so it was full of nutty flavor and it had a nice subtle spiciness because it also contained ray oil, but the sauce was so good. The taste is good because it has a savory flavor, but it is unfortunate that the dried pollack flavor of the dried pollack dumplings is relatively obscured and cannot be easily felt, but the dumplings themselves are moist and good.

However, I think that if you want to better enjoy the natural taste of dried pollack dumplings, a less spicy sauce would be better.

I quickly emptied 5 pieces of pollack rolled dumplings and this time I turned to the yellow gomtang, which felt like a signature menu item. There was a film on top of the yellow gomtang. The explanation on the counter said that it was made from natural protein. When I tasted the soup first, it was a gomtang with a rich pollack taste and aroma. It felt like it was definitely higher quality than other dried pollack soup restaurants I've been to, and it felt like a health food, which made me smile.

It has enough umami that I can eat it on its own, but I added about 2 teaspoons of domestic shrimp paste to season it, and it was just right. I don't like spicy food, so I didn't add Cheongyang pepper, but just sprinkled some pepper. I rolled the rice and tasted it. There was quite a bit of dried pollack in it. The texture of the dried pollack was just right, not too soft or stiff, and the taste was also high-end, so I finally like Hwanggomtang, a high-end version of pollack soup. I feel like we met.

The side dishes consist of radish radish kimchi, pickled mustard greens, and salted fish that give off a Korean feel at first glance. Although the radish radish is slightly below the high standard of what you get at a good seolleongtang restaurant, it is subtly sweet.
I can feel it, it's a style these days, but it's good in its own way. The pickled mustard has a taste that reminds me of slightly stir-fried kimchi, but it's bitter and slightly spicy, so it's still good in its own way.

Seedjeotgal, which is made with squid, octopus, herring roe, and various seeds, is also good because it is not salty and has a rich, nutty taste.

It tasted like a rich health food, so I drank it to the last drop. He asked me if I had eaten it all, and when I saw that they were serving dessert, it was green tea ice cream with soybean paste sprinkled on it. The texture of the green tea ice cream was a bit disappointing as it wasn't as good as Haagen-Dazs, but it had to be this.

He said he was grateful because it was so clean, so I said thank you for the delicious meal and left the store.

I generally like dried pollack and pollack, so I stopped by a restaurant that said their pollack soup was good, but it was less good than I expected. However, when I tasted this restaurant, the rich yellow gomtang taste felt like a health food, and it tasted good. I ate it deliciously. It felt like a health food, so it felt like they opened a store in front of Soonchunhyang University Hospital. It was a pleasant visit that I thought I would stop by again in the future if I want to eat yellow gomtang.

reviews.author: Bobby Choi
reviews.text:
Although the bustling streets that once filled the streets of Itaewon are no longer what they used to be, talented chefs are still challenging Itaewon with food with their own unique colors. I cautiously suspect that ‘Haveu’ may also be a space born from such a trend.
If this is your first visit, it may be a bit difficult to find because it is located inside an alley. But the moment you open the door and enter, the effort is quickly rewarded. The wide open windows and calm interior colors make you feel at ease, and the structure where guests sit around a long bar table facing the kitchen provides a unique pleasure. Tables are also available for guests who wish to sit across from each other. Thanks to the neatness felt throughout the space, there is a natural expectation that the food will also be simple and hearty.
Hevu's food is a fusion cuisine based on authentic Korean food. At first, I was curious about the fact that although it was Korean food, rice was not provided separately, but the moment I took a bite, all my doubts disappeared. Overall, the seasoning is not excessive, and the freshness of the ingredients is clearly evident. In particular, the tteokbokki was a taste familiar to everyone but was of high perfection, and the potato pancake with lecola had an impressive taste with an unexpected combination.
I visited three times and tried all the dishes on the menu, and none of them were made in a sloppy manner. You can feel the care put into each plate, and the side dishes that come with them also have a familiar yet new charm. Another big advantage here is that you can enjoy ‘luxurious taste’ at a reasonable price. What's most impressive is that the owner personally serves the food and takes great care to ensure that even a single visit is a special experience.
As I leave the store and leave behind the owner's friendly goodbye, I feel natural happiness in the harmony created by food and service. It's a quiet, yet deeply impressive place, and it's a hidden gem in Itaewon with a clear reason to want to come back again.

190414 visits
It's a great restaurant. It's worth taking the time to go to Itaewon just for the barbecue pork belly here. It's a three-story building, so you can get in quickly even if there's a wait. I visited around 8pm late on a Sunday evening and it was spacious. I ate the signature menu, barbecue pork belly for two, air rice, and kimchi fried rice (I also had a bottle of Cass).
The pork belly is first prepared and the staff cuts it and grills it for you. Green onion salad, bean sprouts, kimchi, and garlic are put on the grill, and the staff also puts them on their own. Other side dishes include ssam vegetables, raw garlic, cut ssam radish, and perilla leaves (the best). Be sure to eat a lot of perilla leaves. It's amazing because it's sweet and salty without being salty.
The pork belly here is made by grilling the first layer of pork with the sauce on it, and the meat is cut into small pieces of appropriate thickness, so the taste is sweeter and softer. If you are looking for pork belly that is thick and has the feel of a large steak, this may not be the place for you. It was a really delicious pork belly restaurant. Hello!

reviews.author: ethan ghymn
reviews.text:
A photo of curry posted on Instagram caught my eye, and I saw that it was curry from a new store called Yokosuka Tsunami, located a little further down the street from Yesterday's Curry in Bogwang-dong, which I often go to and like. I saved it as a place I wanted to go and stopped by today during lunch time.

It was so hot today that it was difficult to go.

I entered the familiar alley, passed Yesterday's Curry, which had moved to the old supermarket across the street, and walked a little further. I saw a store next to the hardware store that was hard to recognize because it had no sign. The exterior of the store has a navy theme with a navy colored awning.

Looking at the menu outside, there were two options: curry and gyudon. Since curry is famous, I decided to have curry. When I went inside, the owner, a tall man with a handsome face, was sitting at the table. He stood up when he saw me.

He had a puzzled look on his face, but when I asked him if he was here to eat, he answered yes, saying that there weren't many customers during the day, and went to the kitchen. It's still a new store, and since it's located in an alley, it's not well-known, so it seems like most customers are still in the evening.

When I asked what I wanted to eat, I asked if they made all the toppings for the curry themselves, and they said yes except for the fried shrimp in breadcrumbs. Instead of the menu posted on the wall, there was a small photo album with a menu, pictures and a brief guide to the Yokos Katsunami restaurant in Yokosuka, Japan. There was also pork cutlet as a topping, so I tried to order Shirase curry with pork cutlet as a topping, but now pork cutlet is not on the menu. He said that there was only cheese pork cutlet and explained that the cheese pork cutlet was the same price, but I don't like cheese pork cutlet, so I just asked for the Shirase curry to be a little spicy. He brought me a seasoning container containing red pepper-like powder and explained that if you add this, it will be spicy and that you can sprinkle it as much as you like. I wanted it to be spicy from the beginning, but I knew that was the way it was done here.

When I sat down, I asked the owner who brought me cold water in a glass bottle and prepared the curry, and he told me that he had worked at the main branch of Yokosuka Tsunami in front of Yokosuka, Japan, which won the grand prize at the Japanese Gourmet Contest for about two and a half years, and that he had received permission from the owner to open a restaurant under the name Yokosuka Tsunami in Korea and would serve the food according to what he had learned there.

After waiting a bit, the Shirase curry I was looking forward to came out, and when I looked at the appearance, I liked the simple and friendly appearance that I like, which is far from the Instagram-worthy appearance of a curry that looks like something your mother would make at a real Japanese home or something you would see in the military.

When I looked at the curry, it contained potatoes, carrots, and onions, and on top were garlic flakes and sliced ​​green onions, and on one side of the curry, Japanese-style pickled radish and pickles were placed together instead of separately. And furikake is sprinkled on top of the rice.When I picked up the spoon and tasted the curry, it had a subtle sweetness. It was not the sweetness I dislike, but the sweetness from carrots and onions, so I liked this subtle sweetness. Still, I like slightly spicy curry, so I sprinkled the red powder from the seasoning box I brought earlier on one side of the curry, and with a skeptical mind, I took a spoonful and tasted it. Wow, it was as spicy as I expected. Wow. I was skeptical because I thought the shichimi in this seasoning container wouldn't have the spiciness I like, but that wasn't the case, and it had exactly the spiciness I wanted. I was surprised and asked what this was, and he said it was a secret seasoning made using imported red peppers. So, I sprinkled it all over the curry and enjoyed it spicy and delicious.

While I was eating curry, I heard the owner frying something in the kitchen, so I thought he was making lunch for me, but instead, he told me to taste it and gave me a quail egg and whole shrimp from the Kansai-style kushiage menu, and a crab meat croquette with long cherry tomatoes as toppings for the curry. Wow... I'm grateful, but I thought he was giving me too much, so he said he was grateful for coming on purpose, but it seemed like he was the type to always give me various things. Since he just started the store, I liked that he wasn't too calculating and was pure.

He said it would be best to eat the shrimp before they cool down, so I quickly dipped the shrimp kushiage in a slightly sweet sauce similar to Worcestershire sauce and when I tasted it, it was very springy. Also, I tried the quail eggs without knowing what they were at first, and I thought they weren't fried onions, but what they were, but when I asked, they said they were quail eggs. As expected, it has an interesting texture and is good because it is fried in fresh oil.

Also, when I took a bite of the croquette, it was a potato croquette that felt slightly grainy, not overly fine like mashed potatoes. I saw something pink and it turned out to be crab meat. It's a slightly grainy croquette that I like, and although it's a different type from the one at Hammubara in Jongno, which I recently visited and liked, I liked this one more when I looked at just the potatoes inside.

He asked me if I didn't have enough curry or rice, but I was already full, so he asked if I would like a cup of plum tea. I said okay, and he said he would give it to me after the meal. When I finished my meal, he gave me some cool plum tea with ice, so I finished my meal neatly and satisfactorily and walked out into the 30-degree sun.

Overall, it is a store that serves a simple, home-style Japanese curry that I like to bet on. As the owner said, it was even better because it had the same look and taste that I learned in Japan, which has not yet been localized, and I really liked it because it is run by a handsome young owner who is pure and compassionate. When I think of curry, I want to stop by here often, as well as yesterday's curry in the same alley.

The Shirase curry, which tastes like a Japanese home-style meal, which I enjoyed on my first visit last time, made me curious about what the grilled beef noodle I had not yet tasted would taste like among the two meal menus, so I visited again today to satisfy my curiosity.

I ordered a large size of direct-fired gyudon, and it came out a little later. The beef and pork belly part of American beef has a sweet and salty taste of rib seasoning that all Koreans would like. It has a torch-seared taste, so it has a fiery taste. The meat itself is good, and the beef and pork belly cut is soft, juicy, and flavorful, so I quickly inhaled it.

Just like the last time I visited, they also let me try a potato croquette and a kushiage made with potatoes that had a rice cake-like texture, which I enjoyed.

From now on, whenever I think of gyudon, I think I will come to this house..

reviews.author: S R
reviews.text:
I am an international student attending a language school! I always like yakitori, but I've been missing it more and more, so I arrived at Tomo in search of a restaurant specializing in yakitori.
To be honest, since I eat Japanese food overseas, I always go there without expecting much, but the chicken skewers here are so juicy and delicious that everyone was impressed. (((The price range is more friendly than Itaewon!))) Tomo's interior is on the 2nd and 3rd floors, and the atmosphere is calm and feels like a hideout, which I really liked.
The clerk also spoke a little Japanese and provided friendly service!
There are many Japanese restaurants in Korea, but this one is one you'll definitely want to visit again!
If you come to Itaewon for sightseeing, I thought it would be a good idea to hang out at a club and then slowly enjoy some yakitori at Tomoro before heading back!
It was so delicious! I can't believe I can find such delicious yakitori in Korea... The price range is also friendly.

reviews.text: I had high expectations as this is a Japanese ramen restaurant with a current Google rating of 4.9, but I was very disappointed. Perhaps because I was the first customer to visit before midnight, the Japanese ramen chashu itself was cold. And the meat that came with the rice was cold. I don't think anyone finds cold ramen delicious. However, as I ate while listening to Japanese city pop style music, I felt like I was in Japan. I think it would be a good idea to give a little more consideration when giving food.

reviews.author: Kai Lee
reviews.text:
Itaewon Back Street Dog Ramen - Order Original Ramen Chashu Rice
This is a place where you will be surprised by the price of less than 10,000 won for ramen and chashu rice together, surprised again by the quality of the store's unique tonkotsu ramen, and finally surprised once more by the hip space inside the store.
Dog ramen is attractive with its Hakata-style rich tonkotsu broth. They say the broth was boiled for over 2000 hours, but it was thicker than expected. The noodles are close to the thin Kata side, but the broth is well-drained and doesn't stick all the way through. There are 3 pieces of chashu and one whole tamago, and it tastes good.
When you're tired of the greasy taste of tonkotsu ramen, the taste goes well with the bright red beni shoga. Halfway through eating, I added some pepper to the sesame seeds that were on the table, so I could enjoy a different taste.
